Fluency in English

Provide expert advice on cardboard displays, floor stands, counter displays, shelf units and other POSM.
Work with a wide range of materials, including cardboard, corrugated board, wood, metal and other complementary materials, in line with the client’s sustainability guidelines.

Manage POSM manufacturers and specialist suppliers throughout the production process.

Build and maintain strong relationships with stakeholders and suppliers.

Nosotros nos hicimos otra pregunta: ¿Por qué seguimos llenando las carreteras de coches con asientos vacíos?
No tenía mucho sentido. Así nació TRIBBU.
Ocho años después, una de cada cien personas en España ya comparte coche con nosotros y superamos el millón de viajes al mes.
Pero esto no va solo de llenar coches. Va de cambiar la forma en la que nos movemos.

jobs.description:
The American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials is currently hiring a Program Manager for Transit Policy, a full-time position located in our Washington, DC office.

Nature Of Position

The Program Manager for Transit Policy manages the policy and technical activities of the Council on Public Transportation, under the supervision of the Program Director for Multimodal Transportation. The Program Manager is responsible for developing and implementing public transportation task force(s) for the Council on Public Transportation and providing transit-related technical assistance to the member state departments of transportation (state DOTs) participating in AASHTO Transit Management (formerly Multistate Transit Technical Assistance Program). The incumbent is responsible for executing the Work Program, which is annually developed by the Council on Public Transportation and the AASHTO Transit Management Steering Committee with input from member states.

The incumbent coordinates communication for the Council on Public Transportation and its task force(s) and for AASHTO Transit Management members through preparation of quarterly newsletter and announcements/alerts as needed, maintenance of the website including update and maintenance of the state directory, and administration of monthly steering committee conference calls. In addition, the Program Manager supports AASHTO Transit Management’s technical activities in coordination with external partner organizations including the Federal Transit Administration (FTA), American Public Transportation Association (APTA), National Rural Transportation Association (RTAP), Community Transportation Association (CTAA) and Transportation Research Board (TRB).

The Program Manager working with the Program Director for Multimodal Transportation and the leadership of the Council on Public Transportation will recruit membership for various task forces in Public Transportation and provide support for and including facilitation of peer exchanges, webinars, and other communications with the task forces.

The Program Manager is responsible for ensuring robust membership recruitment, renewal, and satisfaction by developing membership kits, conducting satisfaction surveys, and administering travel and logistics for two national conferences and other meetings with input and assistance from the AASHTO Transit Management Steering Committee. In addition, the incumbent is responsible for monitoring the AASHTO Transit Management program budget and individual state Travel Accounts.

Additional activities may be assigned by the Program Director for Multimodal Transportation and/or by the Policy Director as necessary. The Program Manager also receives direction from the Council on Public Transportation and AASHTO Transit Management leadership and ensures responsiveness to members’ needs.

Position Requirements

The successful candidate will have a minimum of six years of professional experience of progressively responsible, with experience working for a state DOT transit agency, Federal Transit Administration, public transit organization, or comparable transportation experience at the federal, state or local level is desirable.

In addition, a successful candidate will have prior experience in project management. A bachelor’s degree is required, preferably in urban planning, public policy, public administration, or another transportation related field. Evidence of a higher degree of professional development, such as postgraduate education, is desirable.

The candidate must possess excellent written and oral communication, research and analysis skills, along with the ability to establish work program priorities and carry them out independently. The incumbent must be sensitive to the needs of multiple members and customers, and have a general understanding of the federal and state transportation policies, regulations, procedures and practices. Additionally, the incumbent must be proficient in word-processing software packages with experience in graphics, spreadsheets and the operation of conventional business equipment.

How To Apply

Applicants should submit a cover letter and resume by Friday, October 23, 2026.

Who We Are

AASHTO is a nonprofit, nonpartisan association representing transportation departments in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico. We represent all transportation modes including: air, highways, public transportation, active transportation, rail, and water. Our goal is to foster the development, operation, and maintenance of an integrated national transportation system that is safe and efficient for every individual. We strive to educate the public and key decision makers about the critical role that transportation plays in securing a good quality of life and sound economy for our nation.

The culture displayed at AASHTO is one of inclusiveness. AASHTO fosters a supportive working environment for staff and focuses on both the professional and personal successes of employees. Additionally, employees benefit from a collective workplace that genuinely cares about them and what they do.

Perks And Benefits

This position primarily reports out of our Washington, DC office located in Metro Center. AASHTO offers employees hybrid work schedules, with remote work up to 2-3 days/week.

The salary range for this position is $80,000 – $110,000.

A 403(b) plan with an automatic 3% employer contribution, and up to 9% match.
Comprehensive health insurance benefits and complimentary employee assistance program (EAP).
A monthly public transit benefit up to $325, covering most or all of your costs to get to and from the office.
Generous leave accrual, starting at 13 days of vacation leave, 18 sick days, and 10 paid holidays – 3 of which can be used as floating holidays.
Tuition assistance up to $7,500 per year for job-related programs and degrees.
Access to an on-site fitness center at no cost to you, with workout classes offered throughout the week.
Flexible work schedules.

From our hiring practices through the entire employee experience, we embrace and celebrate the unique experiences, perspectives and cultural backgrounds that each employee brings to the workplace. Monitor developments in the field to identify emerging needs, gaps, and opportunities for driving ambitious climate action.

The American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials is currently hiring a Program Manager for Transit Policy, a full-time position located in our Washington, DC office.

Nature Of Position

The Program Manager for Transit Policy manages the policy and technical activities of the Council on Public Transportation, under the supervision of the Program Director for Multimodal Transportation. The Program Manager is responsible for developing and implementing public transportation task force(s) for the Council on Public Transportation and providing transit-related technical assistance to the member state departments of transportation (state DOTs) participating in AASHTO Transit Management (formerly Multistate Transit Technical Assistance Program). The incumbent is responsible for executing the Work Program, which is annually developed by the Council on Public Transportation and the AASHTO Transit Management Steering Committee with input from member states.

The incumbent coordinates communication for the Council on Public Transportation and its task force(s) and for AASHTO Transit Management members through preparation of quarterly newsletter and announcements/alerts as needed, maintenance of the website including update and maintenance of the state directory, and administration of monthly steering committee conference calls. In addition, the Program Manager supports AASHTO Transit Management’s technical activities in coordination with external partner organizations including the Federal Transit Administration (FTA), American Public Transportation Association (APTA), National Rural Transportation Association (RTAP), Community Transportation Association (CTAA) and Transportation Research Board (TRB).

The Program Manager working with the Program Director for Multimodal Transportation and the leadership of the Council on Public Transportation will recruit membership for various task forces in Public Transportation and provide support for and including facilitation of peer exchanges, webinars, and other communications with the task forces.

The Program Manager is responsible for ensuring robust membership recruitment, renewal, and satisfaction by developing membership kits, conducting satisfaction surveys, and administering travel and logistics for two national conferences and other meetings with input and assistance from the AASHTO Transit Management Steering Committee. In addition, the incumbent is responsible for monitoring the AASHTO Transit Management program budget and individual state Travel Accounts.

Additional activities may be assigned by the Program Director for Multimodal Transportation and/or by the Policy Director as necessary. The Program Manager also receives direction from the Council on Public Transportation and AASHTO Transit Management leadership and ensures responsiveness to members’ needs.

Position Requirements

The successful candidate will have a minimum of six years of professional experience of progressively responsible, with experience working for a state DOT transit agency, Federal Transit Administration, public transit organization, or comparable transportation experience at the federal, state or local level is desirable.

In addition, a successful candidate will have prior experience in project management. A bachelor’s degree is required, preferably in urban planning, public policy, public administration, or another transportation related field. Evidence of a higher degree of professional development, such as postgraduate education, is desirable.

The candidate must possess excellent written and oral communication, research and analysis skills, along with the ability to establish work program priorities and carry them out independently. The incumbent must be sensitive to the needs of multiple members and customers, and have a general understanding of the federal and state transportation policies, regulations, procedures and practices. Additionally, the incumbent must be proficient in word-processing software packages with experience in graphics, spreadsheets and the operation of conventional business equipment.

Our goal is to foster the development, operation, and maintenance of an integrated national transportation system that is safe and efficient for every individual. We strive to educate the public and key decision makers about the critical role that transportation plays in securing a good quality of life and sound economy for our nation.

Sequoia Climate Foundation is a climate philanthropy that believes in a world powered by clean energy, where all people are protected by policies that have averted the worst effects of climate change. Job Summary

The Program Manager develops cutting-edge, evidence-based grantmaking plans designed to achieve transformational and lasting change in support of the Grids and Data & Research portfolio's impact goals. Reporting to the Vice President, Programs, the Program Manager works closely with cross-functional teams, bringing an entrepreneurial, hands-on approach that seamlessly blends strategy with direct technical execution.

Operating with a high degree of independence, the Program Manager applies systematic thinking to conceptualize and steward complex grantmaking strategies. Sequoia’s grids portfolio works to evolve the way that grids around the world are planned, built, and operated to support a clean energy future. The Data and Research program supports open access models and data systems to enable accelerated clean energy deployment. By holding the vision for the two portfolios individually and as a whole, the Program Manager ensures that our grids and data & research grantmaking reinforce one another to maximize complementary impact.

Working across Sequoia Climate Foundation and with grantee partners, the role assesses emerging needs, gaps, and opportunities and collaborates with peer networks, policy officials, and thought leaders in the field.

Essential Job Functions & Key Outcomes

Support all aspects of strategy execution and strategic priorities, and set operational plans by conducting research and analysis on specific programs and climate sector trends.
Work closely with internal Sequoia teams to bring grantmaking forward to approval level, developing and articulating theories of change, helping to estimate emissions reduction impacts and managing grantmaking processes that involve setting forward workstreams linked to real world outcomes.
Support grantmaking portfolios, including initial screening of potential grantees, analyzing background information, soliciting, developing funding proposals, building and managing grantee relationships, advising on appropriate funding levels, preparing docket materials, monitoring and stewarding active grants, and preparing grant recommendations. Description & Requirements

AESC is looking to add a Project Manager to our team.

About AESC US LLC

AESC is an exciting, newly created global organization committed to solving the challenges of a sustainable future and becoming the leading supplier of full-value-chain battery solutions. Our lithium-ion batteries can be found in nearly one million electric vehicles worldwide and have a stellar safety record of zero-critical issues. AESC US is leading the way in battery technology. We design and manufacture EV battery technology for various electric vehicles and equipment. We are working hard towards unlocking the full potential of sustainable energy and climate change mitigation. We will continue to build upon our successes and expand into new markets and industries, producing innovative and competitive products and technologies that advance the goal of a zero-carbon emission future. AESC is headquartered in Japan and has battery manufacturing locations in Japan, UK, China, and the U.S.

AESC Mission

Our mission is to solve the challenges for a sustainable future. Together, we can make a meaningful impact.

About The Role

We are seeking a detail-oriented and highly organized Project Manager to support the execution of utility-scale energy storage and infrastructure projects. This role will focus on project administration, scheduling, documentation, and internal cross-team coordination to ensure smooth delivery of complex projects. The Project Manager will work closely with sales managers, engineering teams, and external stakeholders to maintain project momentum from initiation through completion.

Project Management

What You Will Do

Serve as the central point of contact for project documentation, scheduling, and reporting.
Support sales managers and project managers in tracking milestones, deliverables, and dependencies.
Coordinate internal resources and external partners to ensure timely execution of project tasks.
Maintain accurate project records, including meeting minutes, action items, and progress reports.
Assist with preparation of project proposals, RFP/RFQ responses, and client-facing documentation.
Monitor project timelines and budgets, escalating risks or delays to senior management.
Facilitate communication between cross-functional teams (engineering, procurement, sales, and services).
Support compliance with organizational standards, safety requirements, and quality assurance processes.

Technical Management

Lead remote commissioning activities for energy storage systems, including system configuration, functional testing, and performance validation.
Act as the technical authority during commissioning, guiding and directing the commissioning team to ensure successful project execution.
Perform and oversee technical service work, including troubleshooting, diagnostics, and repairs for energy storage systems.
Provide advanced technical support for service issues and collaborate with engineering teams to resolve complex challenges.
Prepare and maintain detailed commissioning and service documentation, including test reports and maintenance records.
Ensure compliance with safety standards, quality requirements, and regulatory guidelines during all commissioning and service activities.
Offer technical training and mentorship to commissioning and service team members.

Qualifications

What You Need

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Project Management, or related field (or equivalent experience).
2–4 years of project coordination, project support, or operations experience; exposure to utility-scale energy, infrastructure, or construction projects preferred.
Familiarity with project management methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, Hybrid).
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Proficiency with project management tools (MS Project, Smartsheet, Asana, Jira) and Microsoft Office.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey technical and commercial information clearly.
Self-driven, detail-oriented, and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment

What is “Nice to Have”?

Knowledge of energy storage systems, renewable energy, or large-scale infrastructure projects.
Understanding of permitting, interconnection, and regulatory processes.
Experience supporting EPCs, utilities, IPPs, or project developers.
Familiarity with CRM platforms and project tracking systems.

What We Offer

Welcome to AESC, supporting our state-of-the-art Gigafactories, where you'll have the opportunity to tackle the world's most fascinating challenges alongside exceptionally talented individuals who are driven to make a difference. At AESC, we offer a comprehensive compensation package. In addition, we provide a range of valuable benefits, such as 401K, and health insurance. We strive to ensure that our employees are well taken care of, enabling them to focus on their work and contribute to our collective mission of changing the world.

An inclusive and diverse work environment that fosters and encourages professional and personal development.
Highly automated, clean, safe, and temperature-controlled production environment
Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance
HSA and Flexible Spending Accounts
401K with company match
Life Insurance (Company paid and additional voluntary life available)

Tuition reimbursement

Opportunity to contribute to large-scale energy transition projects impacting grid reliability and decarbonization.
Hands-on exposure to complex, high-value infrastructure projects.
Comprehensive training in project management methodologies and energy storage technologies.
Career growth opportunities within project management, operations, or commercial functions.
Comprehensive benefits package including [health insurance, retirement plan, PTO, etc.].

Even if you don't meet every requirement listed, if you believe this role suits you well, we encourage you to apply. Your application gives us the opportunity to learn more about you and explore potential fits within our team.

Following the submission of your application, we are committed to providing timely responses to all applicants, though response times may vary depending on the volume of submissions. If you do not receive an immediate response, please rest assured that this in no way reflects on the quality of your candidacy. Your application will be retained in our files, and we may reach out to you for future roles that align with your skills and interests. As our organization experiences rapid growth, we appreciate your patience in this process. We are actively working each day to enhance our application procedures to ensure a smoother and more efficient experience for all applicants.
